- **self**: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings (11/4)

## Definitions

- [statement] Cache size scales with num_ctx and is not changed by weight quantization. For llama3.1:8b at f16 the cache is about 128 KiB per token: 4 GiB at 32,768 tokens, 8 GiB at 65,536; q8_0 at 32,768 tokens is about 2.13 GiB. Sliding-window or shared-KV models (Gemma family) break this formula, so sum the 'llama_kv_cache: size' log lines instead. (low confidence) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings

## How it works

- [statement] OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION is automatic by default: Ollama uses Flash Attention when the selected backend and devices support it. Setting OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 forces it on and OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=0 disables it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings · also: https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A quantized K/V cache requires Flash Attention. Without it the runner rejects a quantized V cache with the error 'quantized V cache was requested, but this requires Flash Attention'. Fix: set OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 explicitly; if the error persists the backend has no flash attention kernel and the cache must stay f16. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE is a global option: every model runs with the same type. K and V use the same type, and the type cannot be set per model, in a Modelfile, via the API or on the command line. For mixed types the SSD Nodes guide suggests a second Ollama instance on another port. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings · also: https://smcleod.net/2024/12/bringing-k/v-context-quantisation-to-ollama/, https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization
- [statement] Quality measurements are early and come from the feature author's blog: on Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B (2024-12-06) perplexity went from 8.3891 (f16) to 8.3934 (q8_0), +0.0043. Early implementation figures were roughly +0.002 to +0.05 for q8_0 and +0.206 to +0.25 for q4_0. The author flags embedding models (Ollama tries to detect them and disables quantisation, with a warning), vision models and high-attention-head models (Qwen 2) as possibly more sensitive. (low confidence) — https://smcleod.net/2024/12/bringing-k/v-context-quantisation-to-ollama/ · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings
- [statement] Hardware support at introduction: Metal on Apple Silicon, CUDA on Pascal and newer, and most ROCm GPUs. If a model or hardware does not support flash attention, Ollama falls back to f16 and logs a warning. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-12-04) — https://smcleod.net/2024/12/bringing-k/v-context-quantisation-to-ollama/ · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings
- [statement] Upstream llama.cpp CUDA builds compiled without GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS can reportedly fall back silently to CPU attention when flash attention is combined with some quantized K/V combinations (reported: q8_0 K with q4_0 V, head size 512), giving 25-45x slower prefill and no warning. The report is one user's setup, was closed 'not planned' on 2026-07-26 and does not name Ollama builds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-26) — https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/24485 · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings

## Facts and statements

- [statement] OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE sets the K/V cache type. Valid values are f16 (default), q8_0 and q4_0. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings · also: https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization
- [statement] Per the Ollama FAQ, q8_0 uses approximately 1/2 the memory of f16 with a very small precision loss (recommended if not using f16). q4_0 uses approximately 1/4 the memory with a small-to-medium loss that may be more noticeable at higher context sizes. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings · also: https://smcleod.net/2024/12/bringing-k/v-context-quantisation-to-ollama/
- [statement] On systemd installs the variables must be set as Environment= lines on the ollama unit, followed by daemon-reload and restart. Exporting them in a shell does not affect the managed server. A restart unloads all models. (medium confidence) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] Verify the settings on Linux with journalctl -u ollama: the 'llama_kv_cache: size' line shows K (q8_0) / V (q8_0), the 'starting llama-server' line shows --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --flash-attn on, and the startup config shows OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE:q8_0. ollama ps shows SIZE and CONTEXT. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization · keywords: Ollama flash attention and KV cache type settings
